decisions.structure: CSharp LlvmRuntimePlatform.Create selects WindowsX64/LinuxX64/Wasm32Browser implementations; virtual platform capability/primitive families supply target-specific code to the emitter. Native target descriptors and entrypoints supply width/architecture/object format/dispatch configuration to preparation and backend emission, while typed/control/ownership providers supply committed values and owners to those runtime consumers.
decisions.branches: COFF/ELF/WebAssembly target and64/64/32-bit pointer metadata; Windows/Linux compute-capable lowering versus browser sequential preparation; Windows BCrypt chunk/status versus Linux partial getrandom progress; WinSock/UTF16 DNS versus POSIX descriptor/byte DNS families; existing capability rejection or browser helper stubs remain separate target contracts.
decisions.logic: Register the downstream platform output consumer responsibility in the frozen CodeGen scopes. This is not a new language expression/control/ownership algorithm in platform adapters. Shared NativeRuntimePolicy data already supplies several runtime families; this unit additionally removes both secure-random fill copies and shares the authoritative nounwind attribute definition. Other OS primitive representations remain explicit dependencies, not newly executed or asserted byte-identical.
decisions.diagnostics: Keep existing target/layout/CPU feature and capability admission. No unsupported branch is silently mapped to another OS. Current Windows secure-random tests and exact helper/group observations qualify only their scope; Linux/browser execution, every OS primitive and complete capability equality remain pending.

decisions.structure: CSharp Dns/Socket/Process/MappedBytes emitters consume canonical stdlib receiver/argument/result types; Drop consumes resulting owner metadata. Native normalizes declaration-owned runtime operations, emits target primitives through platform_io and preserves matching canonical values/resource kinds in typed IR and ownership/drop consumers.
decisions.branches: DNS bounded32-byte endpoint descriptors and owned endpoint array versus typed error; socket/completion handle and buffer receivers; Child cached wait state versus OS wait; borrowed text/bytes with null backing versus owned mapped/source backing; mapped non-null release, socket/child lifetime paths.
decisions.logic: The registered correspondence is value/owner input and downstream consumption. Platform-specific calls and failure protocols remain in the existing primitive emitters; canonical receiver/type/source/owner conditions are not replaced by source spelling or a default value. Secure-random byte ownership and scalar output exercise current Windows integration, not every resource family.
decisions.diagnostics: Preserve argument/arity/port/receiver/result checks, bounded DNS/host limits, process capability errors and canonical drop guards. No newly executed DNS/socket/process/mapping, live network, ownership phase or final platform acceptance is inferred from these source links.
